I've played this game a lot. As of this review, I only have 3.7 hours played on Steam but in that time I speedran all the achievements in my save. I played the game when it was released on EGS originally and in that version of the game I completed everything on the to-do list in all three saves. It's an absolute blast.

The mechanics are simple and the game is very forgiving. You can pick stuff up with your beak, flap your wings, run, and crouch, and honk. You will have to use every mechanic in your playthrough but nothing on the initial to-do lists is overly difficult. There are no time limits and there is no fail state. You can get chased out of areas, have your progress undone by the NPCs, but you are always able to keep going.

Furthermore, the entire game's tone is playful (mostly) harmless mischief. You will have some great laughs playing and feel genuine satisfaction when you finish some of the objectives. It's overall a blast.


Once you finish the main set of todo lists the game will provide you with two new todo lists that involve traversing the entire game world to complete, using the mechanics and manipulating the NPCs in fun and interesting ways. Some of these are a lot more challenging and tricky to figure out but still very manageable and satisfying to complete.

The final set of tasks is to complete the games initial to-do lists in under six minutes. These will really put your skills to the test and require a lot of careful planning and good timing to accomplish. Don't mistake these objectives for competitive speedrunning though, with a bit of planning as described and a solid grasp on the mechanics everything should be doable for the average player... after enough attempts.


All in all, a very fun experience, highly recommended. I haven't even tried the coop mode yet either, I'll bet that's a lot of fun. Please play this game!

Untitled Goose Game is a charming and mischievous experience that offers a unique blend of stealth and puzzle-solving. Set in a quaint little village, players take on the role of a troublemaking goose, causing chaos for the unsuspecting residents. The game's simple yet engaging premise makes it easy to pick up, while its humour and creativity keep it entertaining throughout. With an emphasis on non-violent mischief, it provides a refreshing change from traditional gaming experiences.
While there is no deep narrative, the game thrives on its emergent storytelling, allowing players to craft their own mischievous tales. Each villager reacts dynamically to the goose's antics, creating humorous and unexpected moments. The objectives, presented as a to-do list, guide players through various pranks, from stealing objects to locking people out of their homes. The lack of dialogue enhances the comedic timing, relying on expressive animations and situational humour to tell its story.
Gameplay is simple yet rewarding, with intuitive controls that allow players to honk, grab objects, and flap their wings to interact with the environment. The puzzle design encourages creative thinking, as solutions often require observing NPC behaviour and exploiting their routines. The open-ended nature of some tasks allows for different approaches, adding replay value. While the game is relatively short, the satisfaction of completing each prank makes every moment enjoyable.
Visually, the game adopts a minimalist, storybook-inspired art style that perfectly complements its lighthearted tone. The soft pastel colours and clean, hand-drawn aesthetic make the village feel warm and inviting, despite the chaos unfolding within it. Subtle animations and expressive character designs bring the world to life, making even the simplest actions amusing. The dynamic music, which reacts to the goose’s actions, enhances the comedic impact, adding to the game’s overall charm.
Overall, Untitled Goose Game is a delightful and inventive experience that thrives on creativity and humour. Its simple yet effective gameplay, charming visual style, and dynamic interactions make it an entertaining adventure from start to finish. While it may be a short experience, its unique premise and endless opportunities for mischief ensure that it remains memorable. Fans of unconventional games will find plenty to enjoy in this quirky and amusing title.
Untitled Goose Game gets a 7/10.

I always thought of myself as a kind, gentle, considerate, and most of all , honest, individual. Or at least I always tried to be.  Then...I became the Horrible Goose, and my hidden "dark side" was revealed. In addition to meet the set goals in the game, the AI is intuitive and open-ended enough that you can make your own game of just creating as much havoc and misery in the village as possible. Annoy, steal, vandalize, and even terrorize the villagers with impunity. All backed up with a musical score based on Debussy's "Preludes", and somehow reminiscent of MisterRogers Neighborhood if MisterRogers Neighborhood took place in an alternate universe where the "beautiful day in the neighborhood" is constantly ruined by sociopathic poultry.
There is some mild violence in some of the tasks, such as making the gameskeeper hit his thumb, and I discovered on my own, you can actually lead the little boy into the lake and make him repeatedly dunk his head underwater.  However, no one dies, and there is no blood. Parents of younger children might need to look at some sample game plays online and see if it is suitable for their kids. As it is, MY kid (who is a millennial adult) introduced me to this game on her Switch. A friend's daughter of a similar age also had a Switch but not many games, so I gave the Untitled Goose Game to her last Christmas.  I only recently got the game for myself once I discovered that it was available for PC, and was on sale.  The game can be relaxing as well because it is so open ended. There are many items in the game that the Goose can interact with, but are not part of the task list.  So far, I haven't tried to "beat the clock" by going through an entire list under 6 minutes, but my only complaint is that there should be a few more suggested tasks. There are some parts of the village you never actually see, such as the actual bell tower (the bell is heard ringing in the game, and the Goose steals the bell from the model village). Despite my joking that the game brought out the worst in me, it really is a cute, relaxing game that would be good as a starter game for people who aren't ready for, or don't want, any complex games.

I played this with my wife together in co-op, and we swung back and forth between laughing out loud and being very annoyed and frustrated by the at times infuriatingly clunky mechanics.

Gameplay is as follows: You are a goose and have to progress through 4 areas (a garden, a street, a backyard and finally a restaurant) by solving various puzzles, usually at the expense of the respective human inhabitants.

We finished the main missions in about 3-4 hours, without consulting any kind of walkthrough at all. It was really satisfying when we finally figured out some of the more complex puzzles, and just being a stupid goose doing goose-stuff and annoy the living sh*t out of people delivered some hilarious situations. The extra missions that open up after you've finished the "main" missions, are much more complex and provide you with roughly another 3-4 hours. Nevertheless, if you just focus on the main missions, you will be finished with this thing in one or maybe two long evenings, especially if you resort to walkthroughs. This is basically the game's biggest flaw besides the wasted potential of an overarching story premise: For a 17 Bucks Indie-Game, UGG is rather short. In addition, there are two or three minor annoyances, like the mission objectives being a little too vague at two or three times. In co-op there is also the problem, that the two geese are only distinguished from one another by the sliiiightly different color-tone of their beaks. This led as often to hilarious situations as it did to outright frustration, when we got mixed up and confused.

One more positive thing to mention is the game's fantastic jazzy piano soundtrack, which accompanies the gameplay perfectly and is basically one of the main reasons why the funny parts are so funny.    

In the end, I have no problems recommending UGG to indie-game-afficionados, puzzle-game- and co-op fans and people who are looking for something different and/or funny. However, I can't see how this thing managed to get 8s and 9s out of 10 from the press and critiques, when it is obviuously flawed, very clunky in certain areas and just too short for its current price, especially when the replay value decreases to near zero once everything is said and done. Waiting for at least 50% discount (like I did) is probably the best way to go.

Verdict:
Untitled Goose Game is definitely a joyful little indie gem that deserves your time and money.

Games like Untitled Goose Game are the reason why I love the Indie space so much. This is a very simple pick up and play kind of game that uses logic puzzles to push it's game-play. It's a very calm experience that takes a creative approach to puzzle solving. This whole game is about experimentation, and most people will get quite a bit of time out of just trying different things and racking their minds on how to complete the next goal. The puzzles themselves felt very fair without feeling too easy. There were plenty of "aha" moments that fire off your pleasure receptors when something finally clicks, yet at the same time, not a single thing ever felt so cryptic that I had to look anything up. It all felt fair, logical, and challenging all in one package, which is everything you could ask for with this type of game.

The main game is pretty short, but there's a post game that is just as long as the main game which should be considered an essential part of this experience. Your replay value will be in the form of said post game, as well as speed running the main game (it's actually it's own challenge). I went through this game in co-op mode with a family member, and it took us 6.8 hours to 100% the game. I'd say that's a pretty decent ride for the asking price, and the experience was memorable. If you buy this game, you're really going to want to come close to that 100% mark to get your money's worth. Without it, the main game really is pretty short.

This next thing is a bit obvious, but because this game is completely centered around problem solving, PLAY IT WITH A CLOSED BROWSER. If you look anything up, you are only robbing yourself of this games experiences. This game is meant to provoke critical thought and encourages experimentation within its environments. Once you know the ins and outs of each puzzle, there really isn't a lot of reason to revisit this title, so don't go ruining it for yourself! You only get one REAL chance to play this game, and it's worth the ride, so buckle up, open your mind, and enjoy it!

A fun puzzle game, where you can live out your wildest sociopathic fantasies - nothing beats untying the shoelaces of a kid to make him trip and fall into a puddle so that you can steal his glasses ♥

It's simple and short but effective - there's plenty to do in that little sandbox, and it's often satisfying to witness the consequences of the chaos you've caused.
The music, while also simple, adapts to what's happening and very nicely sets the light-hearted, comedic atmosphere.

The only two real snags I encountered were that some puzzles have only one (sometime convoluted) solution, which is a shame to see in a sandbox game - you're left wondering why your other attempts failed when they're only as much convoluted if not more sensical than the predefined solution. But that's not felt too much, especially given the freedom you have to actually implement the solution.

The other snag is that as a completitionist, I heavily dislike speedrun achievements. Especially in a game like this one. Those were my biggest moments of frustration with the game - nothing like having to go quickly to highlight all the little imperfections in the game and how they're hampering your efforts. But thankfully they're not too bad to go through.

All in all, an enjoyable game, elegantly combining puzzles, sandbox, and sociopathy into a devilish goose simulator 🦢

Everybody knows the goose. You honk, you terrorize a small English village, you honk again, and you solve puzzles. And then you honk again. 

"Untilted Goose Game" is a quaint little puzzle game. The graphics are simple, the audio works, and the puzzles are not very challenging. The game can be beaten in 3 hours. The achievements come fast, and some of them are novel enough to be worth attempting, if only for the zany antics you'll get into. 

I like the game, and I'd recommend it.... just not on PC. I use a standard Xbox 360 controller on a Windows 10 machine. The controls in the game are awful at times. Some of the puzzles require very precise movement or timing, and a control scheme akin to infamous ice world levels from NES platformers is not meant to be a compliment. 

Do the positives outweigh the negatives, especially at a Steam Sale price point? Yes. 
Would I play the game again? Probably. It's fun for a weekend.
Would I play it again on the PC port instead of the Switch? Heck no.

Since my "Not Recommended" rating for "Untitled Goose Game" is based on my personal preference instead of anything intrinsic in the game, I'll start with that.  Simply put, I'm not recommending it because I just don't like games that are filled with fiddly, persnickety, tightly timed activities.  And, that's what this game is.  Now, if you happen to LIKE that kind of game, then this game's for you.  Technically, it's very well done with decent graphics (for what it is).  As long as you remember that you're just a goose whose sole ability is to move things to irritate people (and not a great, all-powerful gamer god), the tasks the game gives you and how they're done are fun and sensible.  And, just watching that goose do things is hilarious.  My only legitimate game complaints are that 1) the game is a bit short (9.8 hours to finish all but the last four (timed) Achievements - so, its list price of almost $20 is too high) and 2) some of the goals you're given aren't well defined (for instance, which character is the "burly man" or where's the "home" you need to take something to?).  Wait for it to go on sale for around $10, and, assuming you don't mind fiddly, timed tasks, then go for it.

This is a quaint and funny little puzzle game that is such a nice time to spend a few hours with. Its minimalist aesthetic and ambient sound design are a perfect match for the small English village in which it’s set. The somewhat isometric viewpoint is also a good match for this environment, highlighting its quaintness, even if the camera can be frustrating to wrangle in some situations. But even with all this quiet charm the game manages not to get stale, thanks to the energy thrust upon it by your antics. Upon starting it up, the game only gives you a list of tasks to complete but in order to cross most of the items off the list you’ll need to get into some mischief. The kind that’ll usually release a burst of frenetic action upon the world, causing people to yell and/or run, items to fall and/or break, and a string of musical notes to fly into your ears. Suffice to say it is immensely satisfying because, after all, how could you not enjoy crossing things off a list AND upsetting stuffy British people at the same time? The tasks themselves range in complexity but there’s never too much frustration in figuring out how to pull them off and so the whole experience strikes the perfect mix between relaxing, intriguing and funny. And to top it all off, the conclusion is pretty much perfect.

And while there’s not much more to say than that, you can also extend your playtime if you’d like by taking on the bonus To Do List that appears after the credits roll. The tasks on it are a very nice inclusion as they’re grander in scope and so require you to move back and forth between every section (which are now completely open to each other) giving you a chance to appreciate the scope and detail of this nice little environment even more. This game is all-in-all a wholly satisfying experience, if you’ve got the patience and temperament for it.

SECOND:
It is frustratingly slow to move the goose around.  Those birds can do a pretty fast sprint when provoked, but not in this game.  

IN CONCLUSION:
Although the graphics are adorable, and the idea is fun, it feels geared more for young children, grandparents wanting to bond with their grandchildren with a game, or those who are completely new to games.

[b] This game is about a goose. A goose that will embark on the adventure of a lifetime, and to help explain what it is like to be a goose, I must provide the history of the goose: [/b]

Geese are found worldwide. They can adapt equally well to hot climates (as long as shade is provided) as to cold climates - as seen in their ability to withstand northern winters out of doors with the minimum of shelter. In spite of this broad adaptability, commercial goose production is only important in relatively few countries in Asia and Europe.

Domestic geese come in a wide range of colours, sizes and shapes. In general, domestic breeds are much larger than their wild ancestors although they have in many cases retained their ability to fly.

There are two main types of domestic geese. The first are thought to have their origins in Europe, descendants of the wild Greylag goose (Anser anser) and the second are thought to have their origins in Asia, descendants of the wild Swan goose (Anser cygnoides). Crosses between the domestic breeds which have originated from these two species of wild geese are fertile and in fact have resulted in a number of recognised breeds.

Over the centuries many countries, and even regions within countries, have developed their own breeds and types of geese. But although there is a large pool of genetic material available for the genetic improvement of the domestic goose, it appears to have been relatively under-utilised. In addition, there are also species of wild geese which could be domesticated or could at least contribute to the commercial goose germplasm. 

For example, from temperate climates, there is the Canada goose (Branta canadansis) of North America and the American Swan goose (Coscoroba coscoroba) of southern South America. From the tropics, there is the Egyptian goose (Alopochen aegyptiacus) from Africa, the Nene goose (Branta sandvicensis) from the Hawaiian Islands, the Bar-headed goose (Anser Indicus) from India and central Asia, the Northern Spur-winged goose (Plectropectus gambensis) from Africa and the Semipalmated (magpie) goose (Anseranas semipalmata) from Australia and New Guinea.

This book will deal only with domestic geese that descended from either the Greylag goose (Anser anser) or the Swan goose (Anser cygnoides).

From the research for this book and a search of its Animal Genetic Resources Data-base, The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) have identified 96 breeds or genetic groups of geese, although there are probably more. Many of these breeds, although important world germplasm resources, are of little direct economic importance today because of their relatively low performance level and/or their low numbers and limited geographic distribution. In addition to these breeds, both old and new, there are a number of commercial cross-breeds made available by companies specialising in goose breeding.

The white Chinese geese have orange shanks, beaks and knobs while the brown variety has orange shanks but its beaks and knobs are black or very dark green. One feature of the knob is that it can be used for sexing at 6-8 weeks of age, if not before. The knob of the male is larger and more pronounced than that of the female. The Chinese goose is relatively small in body size with mature males averaging 5.0 kg and females 4.0 kg. However, the breed is known for its high egg production and there are reports of Chinese geese laying up to 100 eggs in a breeding season of approximately five months (February to the end of June) although 50-60 eggs is the average. Egg weight, at 120 g, is lighter than for most other breeds.

Because the body conformation and meat yield of the Chinese goose is not as good as that of other breeds, it has not been widely used for meat production, either as a pure breed or in breeding programmes as a female line to produce a crossbred commercial goose. However, a number of breeds of geese have been developed by combining Anser anser type with Anser cygnoides type, using the Chinese goose as described here.

The Chinese goose is reported to be very effective as a guard animal. In addition it has strong legs and when required, can range over large distances to forage. This may explain in part why the distribution of this bird extends beyond the borders of China and why they are commonly found in countries like Siberia and India.

You play as a goose who is supposed to terrorise the local townspeople. Sadly however, due to the way that most of their AI works, you are forced into a more stealthy play style (personal pet peeve of mine when gaming, but whatever). You will really learn to hate said townsfolk too, as for the most part they easily outrun you and push you around on contact, which causes you to drop whatever item you're carrying in your beak. Depending on what goal you're trying to achieve, they can also just fuck you up by standing in a certain spot for a period of time, forcing you to just stand still and wait for them to move on. 

The area based goals are put on the table as puzzles, but they ultimately come off more as a “learn how to follow the script” type affair. I like puzzles that give you some input to work with so that you can work towards an output, but a lot of these goals don't really give you any input to work with. It's very much a brute force learning experience – once you figure out how to get the gardener to bend over, you can probably figure out how to steal his keys for example – but even then it won't be easy because of how the AI works. You might be able to grab his keys, but getting away from him is another deal altogether.

Somehow though, despite the play-style enforcing AI, the real villains of this game are the camera and the keyboard and mouse controls. Hold M1 to move and double click M1 to run? A camera that moves based on NPC location regardless of what goal you're aiming for? Bullshit. I eventually found myself just holding A the whole time to be zoomed out because the close camera (default) was impossible to use. And speedrun based achievements? ight imma head out

The art direction is top notch on every level of detail, painting a picture of a classic English town reminiscent of clay-motion children's shows like Wallace and Gromit. The character controller and animations feel extremely satisfying, and overall I get the idea that the devs at House House knew [i]exactly[/i] what they were going for. Clocking in at 5 hours, the game respects the player's time, and I actually enjoyed every last minute of it. 9/10

[i]It's a lovely day in the village, and you are a horrible goose. In what ways will you create havoc today?[/i]
Looking at the initial full price tag, I had doubts whether or not it would be worth it for a puzzle game, so I waited patiently for it to come on sale. After 18.6 hours on record, I feel bad for doubting it. Developers [i]House House[/i] have really turned up the charm with this well-crafted, stealthy adventure. 

Pros: 
- You get to play as a goose. What's there to dislike? 
- There is a [i][b]honk button[/b][/i]!! 
- There are SO many items to pick up / drag / push. Each one seems to carry weight and the appropriate dimensions, as well. The goose can drag a rake, which seems realistic, as I can't imagine even the strongest goose being able to pick up and carry a rake of that size! 
- The environments are beautiful. The game uses quite a basic colour palette, and is very simplistic and soft with its design,  but this does not stunt its beauty. 
- It is genuinely endearing, as a British person, to see what I would presume is a British village portrayed it all its sweetness. The "traditional" English village charm is getting more and more rare these days. If I'm wrong, please put me right! 
- I'm rubbish at stealth-based games, but I managed to 80% (I am [b]NOT[/b] good enough for the 'speed run' challenges!) complete this game. It's absolutely still a challenge, however! 
- I love the design of the humans! They're very 'Animal Crossing'-esque, with the same softness and charm about them as the rest of the game. 
- The human AI is fantastic and really puts you on your guard. Be careful when completing certain tasks - if you draw them too near, they will remember where their lost item is and come to retrieve it! 
- The game's replayability is surprising. If you were worried about this game being a one-play wonder, let me comfort those worries. Completed all the initial tasks? Great - you get more! Is that not enough for you? Game set and match - the devs dare you to complete each area in under six minutes. A great challenge for speed runners! 
- The controls are able to be remapped in the settings, and there is controller support, if a mouse and keyboard isn't your thing. 
- [b]LOCAL CO-OP![/b] How many games have this nowadays? 
- Stuck indoors? Have no real friends? In the middle of a global pandemic? Use Remote Play Together to be a pair of horrible geese with a friend! It is SO much fun (just make sure your Internet is up to par!). 
- No death, no scares, no nastiness - just a goose in a village causing chaos. 

Cons: 
- A few - very few - of the puzzles are a little hard to work out how to complete. 
- Might just be me, but I wish there were other animals you could interact with in this game. 
- The initial game is very short, especially if you're good at these kinds of games. Maybe this opens up the devs to the possibility of future updates / DLC? I'd buy it! 
-One of the extra tasks made me want to throw my laptop into a canal. I'm looking at you, football. 

Overall, this is a definite YES! I love this game, and all the wonderful absurdity that comes with it. The dev team should be very proud of themselves, and all the attention this game gathered. Just remember... 
[i]Mess with the honk, you get the bonk.[/i]

Untitled Goose Game is a simple, silly game that is relaxing to play whenever you have time. This game is just very nice to sit back, relax, and play. No matter if you have already finished the game and play it for the tenth time, you might still discover new innovative ways of making the villagers miserable as a goose. It now features coop as well which means double the fun.

So usually, I like to play a game a bit more before I recommend it, but I knew as soon as I saw the page on the steam shop that I had to own it and after an hour or so of playing it with my brother (and both of us in pain from laughter) I knew it was a keeper!

The tone and visual style of the game is similar to Donut Country or Katamari Damacy: you are essentially ruining people’s lives in a fun and droll way, immersed in a quirky and somewhat minimalist environment; the play style of the game is more like a brain-teaser: like those old point-and-click games, if you can figure out the fractured logic of the game, with a little practice, you have a lot of fun!  The objectives range from the simple to the mind-boggling complex and there are plenty of secret achievements that reward you for experimentation and thinking outside the box.

Of course the game is not perfect and my only real complaint so far is about the controls.  The goose handles like a bowling ball covered in molasses and the initial controller bindings of ‘A’ being for running and ‘B’ for item manipulation is pretty much the opposite of what I got used to playing Final Fantasy games for 20 years.  Fortunately, the button assignment can be changed and, again with some practice, the directional movements can be acclimated to without too much detriment to the overall game.

Anyway, I am always on the lookout for innovative games with unique styles and I definitely love a good laugh... and this game has those things in spades (pun intended--check out the groundskeeper in the first area).  Therefore, especially if you want a humorous break from the usual “kill all the enemies” kind of game, this game comes highly recommended!  Hail the “horrible goose” (which I think should have been the name of the game, but whatever)!  Would honk again!

A joy to play through from start to finish. To be a goose is to be an unpleasant, nonchalant part of nature. Geese themselves are not pleasant to be around, but to be one of them is to be free of the burdens of society that make day-to-day living tedious. Gone are the shackles of other peoples feelings and concerns. In their stead are their hilarious reactions to the chaos committed by the goose. The comedic-yet-stabby piano music that accompanies the player through the game is a character in and of itself. The graphics, simple enough to let the imagination fill in the details. This game is nothing short of a leisurely walk through the park with a pocket full of loud fireworks to throw at the feet of people just trying to enjoy a quiet day. 10/10

People complain UGG is only a couple hours, but that seems prudent given what it is. I'm going to give it a thumbs up because both the game and the goose are charming and beautifully done, and this is a wonderful concept...

That being said, the puzzles get slow and tedious after a while because even at a run the goose (rather accurately, I might add) waddles in a slow and awkward fashion. There are extra tasks to do after you win, and I was like, oh god no.

So that's a fail for fun after the novelty wears off. But I think the game still deserves its price because it's been so beautifully executed.

Before I played this game, from what I saw in the videos on the store page, I thought Untitled Goose Game is like Goat Simulator that players just mess around and make pranks to hooman. Turned out it is actually a puzzle-solving game. I do think the tag puzzle needs to be the popular tag as now it is not, just to make things clear.

Anyway, puzzles in Untitled Goose Game can be categorized as physical puzzles that require you to perform certain actions to crack them, as the opposite of the “traditional” puzzle that does not have action requirement. You really need some subtle and swift controls to proceed especially if you play alone. However, control of this game feels clumsy. On one hand, I think the dev made control in that way on purpose, just like Resident Evil 4 and 5 in order to make the game more intense. On the other hand, there might be some technical reasons as an indie developer. Such as hitbox is not very accurate, the end of objects can be trapped by some small obstacles etc. But I don’t think they are big issues.

What I don’t like is the cumbersome default key biddings. Not sure why but it is completely unlike what PC players get used to. Also, originally developed as a console game, the game does not feel right using keyboard and mouse, although I made it through with mouse and keyboard as I don’t have a controller on my hand. Using a controller is highly recommended.

As for the puzzles themselves, I don’t really like how the puzzles are designed to solve. Many of them are explicit, which are fine, but some are just reasonless. I mean, how to solve them doesn’t really have a clear logical connection with our common sense. They are something so unexpected that are just specific in this game. Plus, because there are so many items in one scene, it is hard to even find clues for them. I get that some people like this kind of puzzles for the unexpected solutions, as well as the funny reaction from the hooman NPC, but I will more appreciate logic-based puzzles that do not deviate much from our common sense.

The game kind of reminds me of Gris that I think they both look really nice, but the actual experience is not that good. I recommend playing in duo mode and with kids might be an even better idea because I think they will be good audiences of the game, and remember to use controllers.

You play as a goose and do what a goose would do: be the biggest dick in existence for your own personal gain.

This game is seriously just dumb and that's where it gets its charm. It's a game about being the wild animal iconic for being an ass to humans... like, how do you get gameplay out of that?? But somehow these "House House" folk have done it. It has a simplistic artstyle, some great humor, interesting puzzles, and plenty of people to piss off. Though this game is really only good for one go as the story remains linear for every playthrough, there are still a bunch of tasks to complete after you beat the game giving you something further to do. Furthermore, if you like speedrunning there's even an entire to-do list for completing each and every stage before the church bell rings (in one consecutive run and there's no fast travel feature; no way to skip a stage and complete the next stage at the beginning of the church bell timer). 

There's a decent amount of content here though it's still pretty small. The playtime recorded for this review is how long it took for me to beat the game (everything I say here is fresh in my head) so don't expect something expansive beyond about 5 stages. There is of course the recently added coop mode where you can play it with a friend and a good dozen or so achievements to unlock in addition to completing the final to-do lists, so if you're willing to squeeze as much out of this game as possible then that $20 is definitely worth it. Otherwise I'd say either wait for a good sale or just avoid it all together if you don't want to pay that much for a 2-hour long experience.

Some might say this is not much play time for the price, but I see why this game has become a Thing, a meme, a phenomenon.  The art work is charming, and it's rather amusing to realise suddenly that what we're playing here is no more or less than HITMAN without the violence and flashy 3D modelling!  This is a stealth game involving theft and combat.  But no one really gets hurt and it's all in good fun.

The eponymous Goose wanders around a delightful little village, causing mischief and mayhem;  the devs set you a challenge in the form of a To-Do list which assigns tasks like "shut the boy in the phone booth," or "drop a tankard in the river".  You have to figure out how to hide, run, and finagle your way around the irritable townspeople to achieve your goals.  The difficulty level ramps nicely, until the end game does feel like an achievement.

I found the mouse/kbrd controls rather difficult for this one, and switched to a gamepad.  Fortunately you can map your gamepad buttons (though not the ToDo List key apparently which is Tab -- I wish the devs would let me map that one to a gamepad button as well, so I could be freed from the keyboard).  The perspective is 3rd person aerial with a bit of zoom, but no other camera control (a bit frustrating at times).  

What makes the game though, is the animation.  The goose's body language (and the humans' too) is naturalistic and comical.  Just watching my goose waddle around brought a smile to my face, before I'd even managed any mischief.

I'd recommend this one for anyone who likes a relaxing, humorous puzzle game.  If you found HITMAN too stressful and violent but enjoyed the stealth aspects, try the Goose!  Extra nice touches are:  human interactions in the Pub scene, the model village which replicates the full size village, and of course the jingling bell in the endgame!  Suitable for anyone from about eight to eighty -- and eminently replayable as the action is so much fun to watch.

Untitled Goose Game is a fun and very funny adventure, puzzle game. So what is the story.

In this game you play as one of nature's most adorable yet evil creatures in the animal kingdom, the ferocious goose and your job is to make everyone else is day miserable and making your day better.

Now let’s talk about the likes. Well to start this, the game’s art style is simple yet beautiful with some nice colors, it feels like a painting. The levels of the game are very nice and fun to explore and finding different items to pick up.

The music in the game is very beautiful; it really sets the mood for the game. The game is all so really cute; I mean playing as a Goose wobbling around picking up stuff and honking is really adorable.

The game’s comedy is very funny and there were legit times where I was giggling as I was being chased. The puzzles are fairly easy nothing too difficult I also liked that in the menu, you can change the way the text looks like one is cursive and the other is regular print.

Now let’s talk about the dislikes. Well the game can be a bit short if you’re not going after achievements. The game's price is also way too high for such a short game I mean 19:99 cents is way, way too high I mean if it was like 10 bucks I would get it, but again 19:99 cents is to high, it’s a good thing it was on sale.

Now with said Untitled Goose Game is a fun and very funny adventure, puzzle game. With simple yet beautiful art, nice and fun levels to explore and very funny comedy. So I recommend this game if you're looking for a cute and funny game, this is for you but say wait till it's on sale.

Untitled Goose Game is one of those games that is purely cathartic, and it's one I keep coming back to when I want to cause goose-powered chaos. It reminds me a bit of Portal, in that the game is mechanically tight, but doesn't overcomplicate itself any more then it has to. It's a good time all around, and certainly worth the asking price.

My one argument against the game is that it's short enough to leave you wanting more of it, even through the additional tasks it gives you once you've completed the main story. In this way, it falls just short of the length of games like Portal, where the game is long enough to feel fullfilling, but also just short enough to not overstay its welcome.

An additional map, or even a small handful of new areas would likely suffice to push the game into that sweet spot. The addition of coop indicates that House House is still willing to put effort into the game, so maybe? Maybe not?

Either way, you'll still have a fun few hours playing the game as is, and I still recommend it.

Untitled Goose Game at its core is a casual puzzle game, but not like any I've played before. The aesthetic is simple but artistic, with prominent music and sound effects.  The graphics and animal-oriented gameplay remind me of Ape Out, but contrary to the brutal battles in that game, here you're just a goose on the loose, causing chaos with no real consequence for mistakes. I can't think of another game where exploration is more rewarding.  It's funny but challenging, logical but silly, just a lot of fun to play. You are, however, rewarded for being methodical and organized, which adds a strategy element.  It's an unconventional game that should appeal to players of a lot of different genres.

Ok, so I know that it's on steam it's been memed to death, there's millions of hours of footage on Youtube on it, and it's probably been reviewed to death.  TL; DR:  Get it, and have fun.

Complicated objectives, simple game.  No guns, just strategy, timing, and lots of honking, dear god the honking.  What makes this game so appealing is that it's not "I have more bullets/better powerups/more weapons" than the baddies, in fact arguably, you're the only baddy (or is it baddie?).

You're a goose, and your only mission is to make life horrible for the township. No blood, no gore, no medpacks, no boss fights.  Just go in, wreck sh*t and have fun doing it.  Learn the game's mechanics and enjoy the simplicity of not having to watch for snipers or that one kid that always pays to win.

Finished the main game in 5 hours, but it's so worth it. I'm still working on the post game lists and honestly I'll probably go back and play the whole thing again eventually. The puzzles are simple enough to not get frustrating (I'm the king of rage quit), but complex enough that my ADHD brain doesn't get distracted (another thing I'm the king of). Highly recommend, especially if you are a troll at heart but don't actually want to hurt anyone. Mess with the Honk, you get the Bonk.
*HONK*

It's been a little while since I played Untitled Goose Game on the Switch, but playing it over on PC did not at all disappoint. Being able to create feathery, honking mayhem with a friend really adds a whole new dimension to the proceedings. While one goose runs distraction, the other gets the goods -- there is still some sneaking necessary, but with a P2 things get much more chaotic and direct. Very much in keeping with the eponymous goose's vibe. 

Untitled Goose Game is very much worth every penny you'll spend on it. It's clear that a lot of love went into this game's creation, and everything about it is highly expressive and finely-tuned. The devs have crafted a world brimming with life and color. No words are needed to convey each villager's feelings towards the intrusive goose -- each one feels unique in their presentation and challenge.  I'm not sure if it's simply the difference between Switch and PC (or if I'm talking out my a**) but the controls felt more responsive. 

10/10 would HONK again

Let me fix the title for you: Annoying Goose Game.
(That's not an insult on the game, you play as an annoying goose; the entire game is you just harassing people as a goose)
---

Functionally you just waddle around stealing peoples stuff and honking at them, making a mess of their area and checking off a list of tasks to move from one area to the next. (drop a rake in a lake, etc)

Is it fun? Yes, but not for very long. After about an hour I'm kinda done with the whole thing. I enjoyed it but can't say that it improves at all from one list of tasks to the next. If you are good at (very simple) puzzle solving you don't have much more than an hour or two of content here and all of it repetitive.

So, where does that leave me? I'd really like to be able to recommend the game. Unfortunately it's way over priced for what's here.

What you see in the trailers and screenshots on the store is ultimately most of the game. Steal a few things, honk at some people, laugh as they get upset. Repeat that gameplay loop while finishing off a simple check list of tasks to annoy them and you're done almost as quickly as you started.

Notice how the swamp of positive reviews (on day one) are all from people with like 10 minutes of play time with nothing better to say than "honk" ? If spending $20 to honk like a goose is what gets you excited, by all means, buy the game and enjoy.

Those types of people could probably also just go stare at a door and bark like a dog and get the same entertainment for free.
---

Bottom line, this is $2 worth of fun with a $20 price tag. I could probably recommend it at $5 or less, but there's no way I can recommend it at $15 to $20.
---

EDIT (2 days later) for additional comment: I've now completed the game twice and have about 6 hours put into it. The achievements don't even trigger reliably. I'm still missing the first area achievement (while I have later achievements that would require the first to be done). 

I don't deny that I had a couple hours of fun, but that just confirms my original value assessment. Good game, bad price. And I feel no incentive to even try playing again until they fix the achievements to trigger reliably since it will just be the same very simple set of puzzles over and over again.
---
